bugs.creator: kevinushey
bugs.summary: as.complex()/as.numeric() on an invalid multibyte string reads past the end (Mbrtowc)

comments.text:
In a multibyte locale, coercing a character string that is not valid in the
locale's encoding -- e.g. as.complex() or as.numeric() of hostile input --
can read past the end of the string. The out-of-bounds read is in Mbrtowc()
(src/main/util.c), which builds a human-readable rendering of the offending
bytes for its error message. Found by fuzzing R with libFuzzer +
AddressSanitizer (oss-fuzz testcase 5931425707393024).

Reproducible example (run in a UTF-8 locale; tested on R-devel r90518,
x86_64 Linux / glibc 2.31 under AddressSanitizer):

    Sys.setlocale("LC_CTYPE", "en_US.UTF-8")        # any UTF-8 locale
    x <- rawToChar(as.raw(c(0xff, rep(0x5c, 300))))  # invalid multibyte bytes
    as.complex(x)
    ## Error: invalid multibyte string at '<ff>\\\...'

On an ordinary build this prints the error above; under AddressSanitizer,
or when the string happens to end near an unmapped page, the rendering
reads past the end of the string first:

    AddressSanitizer: SEGV on unknown address (wild-addr-read)
        #0 utf8_internal_loop_single       (glibc iconv)
        #2 __mbrtowc                        (glibc)
        #3 Rf_mbrtowc                      src/main/util.c:1627
        #4 Rf_isBlankString               src/main/util.c:453
        #5 Rf_ComplexFromString           src/main/coerce.c:281

Analysis:

ComplexFromString() calls isBlankString(), which for the multibyte case
calls Mbrtowc(&wc, s, R_MB_CUR_MAX, ...). On the invalid bytes mbrtowc()
fails, and Mbrtowc() renders the string one character at a time for its
error message:

    for(p = s, q = err; *p; ) {
        if(p > s) used = mbrtowc(NULL, p, n, ps);   /* n from the caller */
        if(used == 0) break;
        else if((int) used > 0) { ...; n -= used; }
        else { snprintf(...); p++; n--; }
    }

n starts at the caller's fixed count (R_MB_CUR_MAX), not strlen(s), and is
decremented in step with p. Once the two fall out of step n underflows to a
huge size_t, so mbrtowc() is told far more bytes remain than actually do,
and glibc's UTF-8 converter copies up to MAX_NEEDED_INPUT bytes into its
own buffer bounded only by that count -- reading past the end of s. When s
ends near a heap page the read faults; otherwise it silently reads adjacent
memory. The fault is not deterministic (it depends on where the string
lands), which is why the oss-fuzz testcase is flagged a one-time crasher;
the over-read itself is present on every call with an oversized count.

Proposed patch: attached as mbrtowc-invalid-string-overread.diff. It bounds
each mbrtowc() call by the number of bytes actually left before the
terminating nul, tracked in a dedicated counter that cannot underflow.

The patch is also submitted as https://github.com/r-devel/r-svn/pull/337,
where CI results (green on all platforms) can be seen.
